text:
ashley: Heads-up — saw a user report where a long-lived cursor (streaming chat session) couldn't resume after its prefix was evicted. Repro on staging.

ashley: root cause looks like we evict prefix -> tombstone removed -> cursor replay expects KV entries and fails with 404 from the read path.

diego: ouch. is this the same as earlier 'cursor vs tombstone' stuff or a new variant?

ashley: related but different. earlier we saw stale reads; this is a read-after-evict where the cursor state is partly in the prefix cache and partly in durable store. eviction removed the fast-path entries and our cursor resume logic assumes they exist.

sam: can you paste the failing logs?

ashley: sure — snippet: ```
[12:02:11.123] CURSOR_RESUME id=cu_9483 prefix=tenant:abc:conv:42 read_status=miss
[12:02:11.124] KV_LOOKUP key=tenant:abc:conv:42:cursor -> not_found
[12:02:11.125] CURSOR_FAIL id=cu_9483 reason=prefix_missing
```

priya: how often are these cursors pinned? iirc long-lived cursors get a soft pin during activity, but idle ones are eligible.

ashley: yes. this one was idle for ~20m (client paused streaming), eviction threshold is 10m on that test pool.

ruslan: options: (A) pin-on-open: keep a light-weight reservation while a cursor exists, (B) checkpoint-to-durable-on-pause: eagerly flush cursor context to durable store so resume reads can pull from durable, (C) on-resume rehydrate: if resume misses, fall back to compact rebuild by scanning event log, or (D) change eviction semantics to preserve minimal cursor keys (meta-prefix).

diego: tradeoffs: A increases memory residency for many idle cursors (cost). B makes pause more expensive and adds write amplification. C is slower on resume (latency spike) but no steady cost. D complicates eviction & increases metadata surface area.

priya: do we have metrics for how many cursors are idle vs active per tenant? would help cost calc for A.

ashley: limited. i ran a quick adhoc query on staging: ~1200 cursors in pool, ~350 idle >5m, ~80 idle >10m.

sam: i worry about pin-on-open for enterprise on Dedicated — tenants with high concurrency could blow memory.

emma: what about a hybrid: soft-pin with decay credits — a cursor gets a small credit bucket when active; credits consumed over idle time; eviction prefers zero-credit prefixes. So infrequent idle cursors still have short protection.

ruslan: that's similar to existing soft-evict credits but per-cursor. Implementation complexity: we currently track credits per prefix; mapping to per-cursor keys means changing accounting and telemetry.

diego: another idea: add a tiny, cheap tombstone-resident metadata object for cursor anchors that survives eviction for N minutes (like 1-2x pause timeout). On resume, the read path sees the anchor and triggers a background rehydrate flow that reconstructs prefix into cache. That keeps eviction cheap but gives fast detection and async recovery.

priya: that sounds promising. need to reason correctness: what if rehydrate races with concurrent writes (cursor resumed and client appends)? we need CAS semantics or epoch checks.

ashley: we can version the cursor snapshot with an 'epoch' token stored in durable store and in the anchor. Rehydrate must validate epoch hasn't changed; if changed, resume logic uses newer durable state.

sam: SLA implications: with async rehydrate the initial resume latency could be 50-200ms (depending on log scan), vs 1-2ms if cache hit. Are we ok with that for hosted customers?

diego: we can tier behavior by plan: hosted free/standard use async rehydrate; enterprise/dedicated can opt into pin-on-open or higher in-memory retention via config. Keeps costs manageable.

emma: operational question: how do we monitor rehydrate failures? add a metric rehydrate_success_ratio and instrument histograms for rehydrate latency and rehydrate-by-cause (evict vs missing-durable). Also add an alert if >1% of resumes require full log replay.

ruslan: implementation sketch for anchor approach: 
- on cursor create/pause: write anchor meta key: `cursor:anchor:<id>` TTL=2m, value={epoch, durable_ptr}
- eviction removes prefix payload but preserves anchor? we can keep anchor as small KV stored in a small-resident slab with different eviction class (meta-slab)
- on resume miss: read anchor; if present, start rehydrate pipeline async and return a 202/resume-pending to client with short polling or webhooks

sam: sticky point: preserving anchor across heavy pressure means reserving some memory slab for anchors; need to quantify size. If anchors are ~64B and we have 10k cursors -> ~640KB, trivial. But if customers have 1M cursors concurrently, that gets bigger. Need limits and overflow policy.

priya: good to prototype. we should also simulate worst-case: large tenants, churn, and bursty resumes. add chaos test that evicts prefixes while many resumes happen.

ashley: proposed short plan: 
1) Prototype anchor-based async rehydrate on staging (diego + ashley) — 2 week spike.
2) Add metrics and traces for resume path + histogram for recovery time (emma) — 1 week parallel.
3) Run load test with synthetic cursors to measure memory and latency (priya + sam infra) — 1 week.
4) If results good, ship as default for hosted with opt-in config for dedicated.

sam: sounds reasonable. escalate if prototype shows >10% resume failures or rehydrate >1s.

diego: volunteer for proto work. ashley can pair on test harness.

ashley: i'll open a tiny RFC doc and link PoC PR to this thread. Also will add a short smoke checklist for rollout (canary on non-critical pool -> increase traffic -> measure).

oncall-bot: Note: created incident playbook pointer -> /playbooks/cursor-resume (auto) :information_source:

ashley: thanks — assigning tasks in the RFC. I'll ping again when PR is up. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all. good tradeoff analysis.

emma: one last note — consider making rehydrate idempotent and rate-limited so noisy resumes don't thrash background workers.

ashley: agreed, add to checklist.

ashley: ACTIONS:
- diego + ashley: prototype anchor + async rehydrate (week 1-2)
- emma: add metrics/tracing changes (parallel)
- priya + sam: load/chaos test plan (parallel)
- ashley: RFC + rollout checklist (today)
